intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to ease into Greek food culture.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival — under €3
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk in Monastiraki — around €2.50–€3.50

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Use the Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki for about €9 — cheapest and fastest option into the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) also covers several other archaeological sites in Athens — great value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, browse the colorful Monastiraki Flea Market for local crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and try mezedes (small shared plates). Walk along Ermou Street for evening people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and salad from a local taverna in Monastiraki — €6–€8
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread at a Psiri taverna — order a few small plates like taramosalata, dolmades, and grilled halloumi — €10–€14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy the €20 combined Acropolis ticket — it covers 7 sites and is valid for 5 days, saving money overall. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Piraeus port and catch an early ferry to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, ~€8–€10 each way). Aegina is one of the closest and most affordable Saronic islands from Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the stunning Temple of Aphaia, one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples. Then head to Agia Marina beach — a beautiful sandy beach with calm, clear water perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by evening ferry and head back to Athens. Enjoy dinner near the port or back in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a café near the hostel — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple taverna near Agia Marina beach — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a Greek salad at a Piraeus portside taverna — €10–€12

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Piraeus port or online. First ferry to Aegina is usually around 7:00–8:00 AM. Bring sunscreen and a swimsuit — the beach is excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a vibrant, authentic local market with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and cheeses. A fantastic sensory experience and very budget-friendly for snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry) — one of the world's greatest collections of ancient Greek artifacts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring treasures including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the bohemian Exarchia neighborhood for an authentic, non-touristy Athens experience. Browse independent bookshops and street art, then find a local ouzeri for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, olives, and local cheese from the Central Market stalls — €3–€5
meals.lunch: Cheap and filling moussaka or pastitsio at a traditional eatery near the museum — €7–€9
meals.dinner: Ouzeri in Exarchia — order ouzo and a selection of mezedes like fried zucchini, fava dip, and grilled sardines — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market is closed on Sundays. The National Archaeological Museum is free on the first Sunday of each month — check if this applies to your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — about 2.5 hours, ~€13. Check into a budget guesthouse in this charming coastal town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town with its Venetian architecture and narrow lanes. Climb the 999 steps up to the impressive Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) for panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Nafplio waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this romantic town and dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee before the bus — €2
meals.lunch: Grilled lamb chops (paidakia) with village salad at a Nafplio taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood pasta or grilled sea bream at a waterfront restaurant — €11–€14

day_by_day.notes: Book the KTEL bus ticket in advance if possible. Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese. The Palamidi climb is steep — go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short local bus or taxi (~€10) to the ancient site of Epidaurus. Visit the remarkably preserved ancient theater — one of the best acoustically perfect theaters in the world — and the Sanctuary of Asclepius (€12 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, scenic rocky beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the crystal-clear Argolic Gulf waters.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nafplio's Syntagma Square in the evening. Try local street food and browse the small shops selling local products like olive oil and honey.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey at a café in Nafplio — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local bakery — tiropita, spanakopita, and a bottle of water — €4–€5
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna dinner — stuffed tomatoes (gemista), tzatziki, and village bread — €9–€12

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus hosts a famous summer festival with ancient drama performances — check if any shows coincide with your visit (tickets from €15). Arvanitia Beach has free entry and is very clean.

day_by_day.morning: Take the KTEL bus from Nafplio to Athens (Kifissos Terminal), then connect to the port of Piraeus. Catch a ferry to Hydra island (~2 hours from Piraeus, ~€18–€22 each way on a Flying Dolphin hydrofoil).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hydra town — a car-free island with stunning architecture, donkeys as transport, and crystal-clear waters. Walk along the harbor and up the hillside paths. Swim at Vlychos or Kamini beach, both reachable on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical sunset over Hydra harbor. Have dinner at a portside taverna before catching the last hydrofoil back to Piraeus and returning to Athens.

meals.breakfast: Cheese pie and coffee at the Nafplio bus station — €3
meals.lunch: Grilled fish of the day at a simple Hydra harbor taverna — €12–€15
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a cold Mythos beer at a portside spot in Hydra — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is slightly pricier than other islands due to its exclusivity, but a day trip keeps costs manageable. Check the last hydrofoil return time carefully — usually around 7:00–8:00 PM. No motorized vehicles on Hydra.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus to Paros island (~4–5 hours by regular ferry, ~€30–€35, or faster by high-speed ferry). Check into a budget room or hostel in Parikia, the island's main town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Parikia's charming whitewashed old town (Kastro). Visit the beautiful Panagia Ekatontapiliani (Church of 100 Doors) — free entry. Relax at Livadia Beach, a sandy beach just a short walk from town.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Parikia's narrow alleys as the sun sets. Enjoy the lively but relaxed island atmosphere and dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee before boarding the ferry in Piraeus — €3
meals.lunch: Fresh calamari and Greek salad at a Parikia waterfront taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb souvlaki plate with tzatziki and pita at a local grill house — €8–€10

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during June as they fill up quickly. Paros is one of the best-value Cycladic islands. Budget accommodation in Parikia ranges from €20–€40/night for a dorm or simple room.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–€25/day) to explore Paros at your own pace. Head to the beautiful village of Naoussa in the north — a picturesque fishing village with a Venetian harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Naoussa, visit Kolymbithres Beach — famous for its unique granite rock formations and turquoise water. Swim and snorkel in the clear Aegean Sea. Continue to Santa Maria Beach for more swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Parikia. Enjoy a sunset drink at a clifftop bar, then have dinner at a local fish taverna near the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Fresh orange juice and a bougatsa (custard pastry) at a Parikia bakery — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Grilled fresh fish and village salad at a simple Naoussa taverna — €12–€15
meals.dinner: Octopus stifado (stew) and a carafe of local house wine at a Parikia taverna — €11–€14

day_by_day.notes: Kolymbithres is one of the most photographed beaches in the Cyclades — arrive before noon to get a good spot. Scooter rental requires a valid license. Fuel up the scooter before returning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short ferry from Paros to Naxos (~45 minutes, ~€8–€10) — the largest and most fertile Cycladic island. Check into budget accommodation in Naxos Town (Chora).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Naxos Town's impressive Venetian Kastro (castle) and the iconic Portara — a massive ancient marble doorway on a small islet connected to the harbor by a causeway. Free to visit and stunning at any time of day.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the atmospheric old town market streets. Sample local Naxian products — the island is famous for its potatoes, cheese (graviera), and citron liqueur (kitron). Dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a cheese pie from a Paros bakery before the ferry — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Naxian graviera cheese and local bread with olives from a market stall — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Slow-cooked lamb with Naxian potatoes at a traditional Chora taverna — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Naxos is one of the best-value Cycladic islands with excellent local produce. The Portara is especially beautiful at sunset — plan to be there around 7:30–8:00 PM. Try a small glass of kitron liqueur — a unique local specialty.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local KTEL bus from Naxos Town to Agios Prokopios Beach — consistently rated one of Greece's best beaches with long stretches of fine white sand and shallow turquoise water. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Agia Anna Beach and Plaka Beach — quieter and more natural stretches of coastline. Bring snacks and water for a full beach afternoon. The bus runs regularly along this coastal route.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Naxos Town for the evening. Browse the old town's small shops selling local honey, olive oil, and ceramics. Enjoy a final Naxos dinner with fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with Naxian thyme honey and fresh fruit at a Chora café — €4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a bakery — spanakopita, fruit, and water — €4–€5 (eat on the beach)
meals.dinner: Grilled sea bass with lemon and olive oil, plus a village salad at a Naxos Town taverna — €12–€15

day_by_day.notes: Agios Prokopios and Plaka beaches have free access. Sun loungers are available for rent (~€5–€8 each) but bringing your own towel and lying on the sand is free. Apply sunscreen regularly — June sun is strong.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry back from Naxos to Piraeus (~5–6 hours by regular ferry, ~€35–€40). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing and relax on deck. Arrive in Athens by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Back in Athens, visit any remaining sites from the combined Acropolis ticket (valid 5 days) — such as the Ancient Agora, Kerameikos, or the Roman Agora. Alternatively, explore the Anafiotika neighborhood — a tiny Cycladic-style village hidden on the slopes of the Acropolis hill.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — head to the Thissio neighborhood for rooftop bar drinks with Acropolis views. Enjoy a farewell Greek dinner in the Plaka or Monastiraki area.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri and coffee at the Naxos port before boarding — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own food or buy a simple sandwich on board — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Plaka taverna — moussaka, Greek salad, grilled halloumi, and a carafe of house wine — €14–€18

day_by_day.notes: Book the return ferry from Naxos in advance. The overnight or early morning ferry options are cheaper but the daytime crossing offers beautiful scenery. Anafiotika is a hidden gem — very few tourists find it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Take a last walk through Monastiraki and pick up any remaining souvenirs — local olive oil, dried herbs, honey, or small ceramic pieces are affordable and authentic gifts. Visit a local café for a proper Greek breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma (~€9, ~40 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories of beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a Monastiraki café — eggs, feta, olives, tomatoes, and Greek coffee — €6–€8
meals.lunch: Final souvlaki wrap or gyros from a street kiosk near the Metro station — €3
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Keep €10–€15 in cash for the Metro to the airport and any last-minute expenses. Greek airports have a departure tax included in most ticket prices. Double-check your flight time and terminal. Καλό ταξίδι — Have a great journey!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Plaka neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll through the charming Plaka district to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market area as the evening crowds gather. Enjoy your first taste of authentic Greek cuisine at a traditional taverna in Plaka.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Taverna Lysikratous in Plaka — try moussaka, tzatziki, and a glass of house wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for the metro ride. Book your hotel in Plaka or Monastiraki for easy walkability to major sights. Exchange some euros at the airport or use an ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to the Acropolis and Parthenon — arrive early (8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Propylaea, Erechtheion, and the Temple of Athena Nike. Allow 2–2.5 hours for the full site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the Acropolis Museum (open until 8 PM) to see the stunning artifacts and friezes from the Parthenon up close. Afterward, walk through the Thisio neighborhood and enjoy a coffee break at a café with Acropolis views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Psyrri neighborhood for dinner — a hip area full of authentic eateries and mezze bars popular with locals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery — try a tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Acropolis Museum — Greek salad and fresh bread (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio (mezze restaurant) in Psyrri — share plates of dolmades, grilled octopus, saganaki, and taramasalata (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Acropolis combo ticket covers multiple sites and costs around €30. Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen and water — the hill can be hot even in June. The Acropolis Museum is air-conditioned and a great midday refuge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens, the heart of ancient Greek democracy, and the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Stroll through the site and imagine daily life in classical Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Piraeus port and catch a ferry to the island of Hydra (approximately 1.5–2 hours by hydrofoil). Hydra is famously car-free — explore the picturesque harbor, donkey-lined paths, and crystal-clear swimming coves.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset drinks at a harbor-side bar in Hydra town, then have dinner at a waterfront restaurant before taking the evening ferry back to Athens (or stay overnight if budget allows).

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near your hotel (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a taverna on Hydra's harbor — catch of the day with lemon and olive oil (€18–24)
meals.dinner: Dinner on Hydra at a traditional restaurant — lamb chops, horiatiki salad, and local wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hellenic Seaways or Aegean Speed Lines run hydrofoils from Piraeus to Hydra. Book tickets in advance online (€30–40 round trip). If returning to Athens, last hydrofoil is typically around 7–8 PM — confirm schedule. Hydra is a wonderful introduction to Greek island life.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Athens — visit the National Archaeological Museum, one of the world's great museums, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold masks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Athens Riviera — take tram line T3 south to Vouliagmeni or Glyfada for an afternoon at the beach. The waters of the Saronic Gulf are warm and clear in June. Rent a sunbed and umbrella and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for dinner — a favorite of Athenian professionals with excellent restaurants and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — eggs, olives, feta, tomatoes, and bread (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Vouliagmeni — grilled corn, fresh juice, and a sandwich (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kolonaki — try a modern Greek restaurant serving creative takes on traditional dishes like slow-cooked lamb with orzo (€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum costs €12 and is best visited in the morning when it's less crowded. The tram to the Riviera is inexpensive (€1.40) and scenic. Vouliagmeni Lake is also nearby — a natural thermal lake worth a quick visit.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Athens (ATH) to Zakynthos (ZTH) — morning domestic flight (approximately 45 minutes, €40–70 with Aegean Airlines or Sky Express). Check in to a mid-range hotel or studio apartment in Zakynthos Town or Tsilivi.
day_by_day.afternoon: **Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Boat Tour** — Join an organized boat tour departing from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed locations. The beach is only accessible by boat. Swim in the turquoise waters beside the famous rusted shipwreck MV Panagiotis, surrounded by towering white limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town and explore the Venetian-influenced harbor area. Walk along the waterfront promenade and watch the sunset over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Athens airport or hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat tour, or enjoy a light meal at a taverna near the port before departure (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a seafood taverna in Zakynthos Town — fresh grilled sea bream, Greek salad, and local Verdea white wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach boat tours typically cost €15–25 per person and last 3–4 hours. Book in advance during June as spots fill quickly. The viewpoint above Navagio is also spectacular and accessible by road — consider visiting at sunset on a different day. Verdea is a unique local white wine found only on Zakynthos.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or car and drive to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos near Cape Skinari. Take a small rowboat tour into the sea caves where the water glows an ethereal electric blue — best experienced in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Gerakas Beach, a protected loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting beach. Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise waters and keep an eye out for turtles. The beach is part of the National Marine Park of Zakynthos.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Zakynthos Town via the scenic mountain village of Machairado. Stop at the village square for a coffee and local sweets before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery — fresh spanakopita and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the beach — pick up local bread, olives, feta, and fruit from a village market (€8–10)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner in Zakynthos Town — try sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce), a Zakynthian specialty (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Caves rowboat tours cost around €10–15. Gerakas Beach has restricted hours in the evening to protect nesting turtles — swimming is allowed during the day. Scooter rental costs approximately €20–30/day; car rental €35–50/day. Sofrito is a must-try dish unique to Zakynthos.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Zakynthos Town itself — visit the Byzantine Museum on Solomos Square, housing rescued icons and artifacts from churches destroyed in the 1953 earthquake. Walk up to the Venetian Castle (Kastro) above the town for panoramic views of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a relaxing afternoon at Tsilivi Beach or Alykanas Beach — both are well-organized sandy beaches on the northeast coast with calm, shallow waters ideal for swimming. Rent a sunbed and enjoy the warm Ionian Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening on Zakynthos — enjoy a leisurely dinner at a rooftop restaurant in town with views of the harbor lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café on Solomos Square — yogurt, honey, and fresh orange juice (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch at Tsilivi — grilled calamari, tzatziki, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Zakynthos Town — fresh lobster pasta or grilled swordfish with local wine (€24–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Byzantine Museum costs €4. The Venetian Castle is free and offers the best views on the island — go in the late afternoon for golden light. Tomorrow you fly to Crete, so pack your bags tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Zakynthos (ZTH) to Heraklion, Crete (HER) — approximately 1 hour (€40–80). Check in to a mid-range hotel or apartment in Heraklion or nearby Hersonissos. Drop your bags and head to the Palace of Knossos, the legendary Minoan palace dating back 3,500 years — one of Europe's oldest and most fascinating archaeological sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, which houses the world's finest collection of Minoan art, including the famous Bull-Leaping Fresco and the Phaistos Disc. Afterward, walk through the lively Heraklion market street (1866 Street) — a bustling bazaar of local produce, spices, and Cretan specialties.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Venetian Harbor of Heraklion and visit the iconic Koules Fortress at sunset. Dine in the old town near Lions Square (Plateia Venizelou).

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Zakynthos airport or hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch at a restaurant near Knossos — dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta), lamb stew, and local raki (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner near Lions Square in Heraklion — try Cretan specialties like apaki (smoked pork), staka (cream sauce), and fresh greens with olive oil (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos entry costs €15. Combine with the Archaeological Museum for a €20 combo ticket. The market street is best visited in the morning or late afternoon when it's most lively. Raki (tsikoudia) is Crete's local spirit — often offered free at the end of a meal.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the **Elafonissi Beach Day Trip** — rent a car and drive approximately 3 hours west to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete. The drive through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) is spectacular. Arrive at Elafonissi, famous for its unique pink-tinged sand (caused by crushed coral and shells) and shallow, warm turquoise lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on Elafonissi's stunning shores. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island of Elafonissi for even more secluded spots. The water is exceptionally clear and calm — perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the scenic drive back east toward Heraklion, stopping in the charming village of Paleochora or Kandanos for a traditional dinner before continuing to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departure — Cretan honey, fresh bread, and cheese (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local market — Cretan olives, graviera cheese, and paximadi rusks (€8–10)
meals.dinner: Village taverna dinner in Paleochora or along the return route — slow-roasted lamb, horta (wild greens), and local wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is essential for this day trip (€35–50/day). Leave by 7:30–8:00 AM to arrive before the beach gets crowded. Elafonissi is one of Greece's most beautiful beaches — absolutely worth the long drive. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snacks. The return drive takes 3+ hours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Samaria Gorge trailhead at Xyloskalo (or take an organized tour bus from Heraklion). Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — Europe's longest gorge at 16 km, passing through dramatic landscapes, ancient ruins, and the famous Iron Gates (Sideroportes) where the gorge narrows to just 3 meters wide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Emerge at the coastal village of Agia Roumeli after 4–6 hours of hiking. Cool off with a swim in the crystal-clear Libyan Sea at Agia Roumeli beach — you've earned it! Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (45 minutes), then a bus or taxi back to Heraklion.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover at your hotel. Enjoy a quiet dinner near your accommodation — you'll be tired but satisfied after the gorge hike.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the hike — eggs, bread, cheese, and fruit (€8–10)
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch for the gorge — energy bars, sandwiches, nuts, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a local taverna near your hotel — simple grilled chicken souvlaki, Greek salad, and cold beer (€16–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Samaria Gorge entry costs €5. The gorge is open May–October. Wear proper hiking shoes — the terrain is rocky. Bring 2+ liters of water per person. The ferry from Agia Roumeli costs approximately €15. Total transportation and entry for the day: €30–40 per person. This is a strenuous but unforgettable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the charming Venetian town of Rethymno (1.5 hours west of Heraklion by bus or car). Explore the well-preserved old town with its narrow alleyways, Venetian loggia, and the impressive Fortezza fortress overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Rethymno's long sandy beach — one of the best urban beaches in Crete, stretching for kilometers along the waterfront. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Browse the old town's artisan shops for local olive oil, herbs, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Rethymno's old town before returning to Heraklion by bus (KTEL buses run regularly, €7–8 one way).

meals.breakfast: Late, leisurely breakfast at your hotel — full spread with Cretan cheeses, honey, and fresh fruit (€8–10)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbor-side restaurant in Rethymno — fresh mussels, grilled fish, and a glass of local white wine (€18–22)
meals.dinner: Old town taverna in Rethymno — try boureki (Cretan zucchini and potato pie) and slow-cooked goat with herbs (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rethymno is one of Crete's most beautiful towns and a perfect recovery day destination. The Fortezza costs €4 to enter. The old town is very walkable. KTEL buses from Heraklion to Rethymno depart frequently from the main bus station. A great day for souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Spinalonga Island — take a morning bus or drive to Elounda (1.5 hours east of Heraklion), then a short boat ride to Spinalonga, a former Venetian fortress and Europe's last active leper colony (closed 1957), made famous by Victoria Hislop's novel 'The Island.' Explore the haunting ruins and fascinating history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Elounda and spend the afternoon at the beautiful Voulisma Beach or Istron Bay — some of the most scenic beaches on Crete's northeastern coast with calm, clear waters. Alternatively, explore the charming fishing village of Elounda itself.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus back to Heraklion for your final evening in Crete. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at one of Heraklion's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Elounda — fresh pastries and Greek coffee with sea views (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a taverna in Elounda — grilled octopus, shrimp saganaki, and fresh bread (€20–26)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner in Heraklion — try a well-regarded Cretan restaurant for a full tasting of island specialties: snails, aged graviera, lamb with stamnagathi greens, and local wine (€28–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Spinalonga boat tours from Elounda cost approximately €10–15 round trip. Entry to the island is €8. The site is deeply moving and historically fascinating. Pack your bags tonight as tomorrow is your final day before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Heraklion. Visit the Heraklion market one more time to stock up on local products to take home: Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, graviera cheese, and local wines or raki.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your return flight time, spend a final hour or two at a nearby beach (Ammoudara Beach is just 5 minutes from Heraklion) or revisit a favorite spot in the city. Head to Heraklion Airport (HER) for your return flight to Athens and onward connection.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories of beaches, ancient history, and incredible food. Safe travels home!

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee (€7–9)
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki or gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the market (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining on the return journey

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Heraklion Airport is small but can get busy in summer. Liquid restrictions apply for olive oil and wine in carry-on — pack in checked luggage. Total estimated mid-range budget for the 13-day trip (excluding flights): €1,400–1,900 per person, including accommodation, meals, activities, and local transport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer by private luxury car to your hotel in central Athens. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through the Plaka neighborhood to begin soaking in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening walk through Monastiraki Square and the illuminated Acropolis viewpoints. Settle into Athens with a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant near the Acropolis — a classic Athenian taverna with rooftop views of the Parthenon; try grilled octopus, lamb chops, and local Assyrtiko wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. No strenuous activities on arrival day. Hotel recommendation: Hotel Grande Bretagne or Electra Metropolis Athens for a luxury stay in the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the midday heat and crowds. Book a private guided tour for an in-depth historical experience covering the Propylaea, Erechtheion, and Temple of Athena Nike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local spice vendors, olive oil producers, cheese mongers, and fresh seafood stalls. Sample cured meats, local cheeses, honey, and freshly baked koulouri with a knowledgeable local food guide.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for boutique shopping and aperitifs at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at a traditional Athenian café — Greek yogurt with thyme honey and walnuts, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and spanakopita
meals.lunch: Lunch during the food tour at a family-run taverna inside or near the Central Market — fresh grilled fish, horiatiki salad, and house-made tzatziki
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Michelin-starred) in Mikrolimano — exceptional modern Greek seafood cuisine with harbor views

day_by_day.notes: Book the Acropolis private tour and food tour in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection — temperatures around 23°C but direct sun can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis Museum (one of Europe's finest archaeological museums) for a deeper understanding of ancient Athens. The glass-floor galleries and Parthenon frieze collection are unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ancient Agora of Athens and Hephaestus Temple, then wander through the charming Thissio and Psyrri neighborhoods. Browse artisan shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Athens International Airport for an evening domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45-minute flight). Check in to your luxury hotel in Chania upon arrival.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh pastries, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Avissinia in Monastiraki — traditional mezedes including dolmades, taramosalata, and grilled halloumi
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri in Chania, Crete — romantic seaside setting with exceptional fresh Cretan seafood and local Cretan wines

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Athens to Heraklion or Chania in advance. Hotel recommendation in Chania: Casa Delfino Boutique Hotel or Villas & Mansions of Crete for a luxury experience in the Venetian harbor area.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class — Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos, lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades with local honey. Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the enchanting Venetian Harbor of Chania — stroll along the waterfront, visit the Venetian Lighthouse, and browse the old town's narrow alleyways filled with artisan shops selling olive wood crafts, leather goods, and local ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a harbor-front bar, followed by a leisurely dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cooking class — Cretan barley rusks (dakos) with tomato and mizithra cheese, and Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as part of the experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Michelin-recommended To Maridaki in Chania — intimate fish taverna specializing in ultra-fresh local catch; try the sea urchin pasta and grilled whole fish

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including market visit. Book well in advance as premium classes fill up quickly. Comfortable shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Elafonissi Beach — Depart early by private car (approximately 1.5 hours from Chania) to visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoon. Arrive early to enjoy the beach before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Elafonissi Beach — swim in the crystal-clear shallow waters, explore the small island accessible by wading, and relax on the unique pink sand. The water temperature in June is perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania by private car. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Venetian harbor area.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel for the beach
meals.lunch: Lunch at the beach taverna near Elafonissi — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer or local rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Portes Restaurant in Chania old town — creative Cretan cuisine in a romantic courtyard setting; try the slow-cooked lamb and local Vidiano white wine

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:00 AM to arrive at Elafonissi before the crowds. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear, and plenty of water. The beach has limited shade so a beach umbrella is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Samaria Gorge (optional hike for active travelers) — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km, offering stunning scenery. Alternatively, visit the Archaeological Museum of Heraklion for those preferring a cultural morning, housing the world's finest Minoan artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the scenic northern Cretan coast to Heraklion. Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace with a private guide to bring the 3,500-year-old history to life.
day_by_day.evening: Fly from Heraklion to Mykonos (approximately 45-minute flight). Check in to your luxury hotel on Mykonos.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Chania — full Cretan spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional kafeneion near Knossos — moussaka, stuffed peppers, and fresh village bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Matsuhisa Mykonos — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion with stunning Aegean views; a signature Mykonos luxury dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Heraklion to Mykonos in advance. Hotel recommendation on Mykonos: Cavo Tagoo or Katikies Mykonos for iconic infinity pool views over the Aegean. The Samaria Gorge hike is strenuous — 6–7 hours; skip if not physically prepared.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) — wander through the iconic whitewashed alleys, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and explore the charming neighborhood of Little Venice where the houses hang over the sea. Browse high-end boutiques and local jewelry shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening — Spend the afternoon at Psarou Beach on Mykonos, one of the island's most glamorous beaches. Enjoy a premium sun lounger and umbrella setup, crystal-clear waters, and the vibrant beach atmosphere. Psarou is known for its calm waters and upscale beach club scene.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a Little Venice bar (Caprice or Galleraki are iconic spots), then dinner at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed juices with Aegean views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nammos Beach Restaurant at Psarou Beach — one of the Mediterranean's most celebrated beach restaurants; try the lobster pasta and fresh sashimi
meals.dinner: Dinner at M-eating in Mykonos Town — award-winning modern Greek cuisine; try the tuna tartare and slow-roasted lamb with truffle

day_by_day.notes: Reserve sun loungers at Psarou Beach in advance — they book out quickly in June. Nammos restaurant requires a reservation. Little Venice is best visited around sunset for magical golden light.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece. Explore the ancient ruins, including the iconic Terrace of the Lions, with a private archaeologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and visit Paradise Beach — the legendary beach known for its lively atmosphere and crystal-clear waters. Enjoy the beach club facilities and a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Mykonos nightlife scene — the island is famous for its world-class bars and clubs. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar before a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with panoramic sea views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Jackie O' Beach Club at Super Paradise Beach — stylish beach club with excellent Mediterranean cuisine and cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spilia Seaside Restaurant — a dramatic cave restaurant carved into the cliffs at Agios Sostis; exceptional fresh seafood in a unique setting

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town — first boat around 9:00 AM. The site has no shade so bring sun protection. Delos is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at your hotel — enjoy the infinity pool, spa facilities, and a leisurely breakfast. Take time to explore any remaining parts of Mykonos Town or do some last-minute shopping for local products (olive oil, honey, ceramics).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ferry or short flight from Mykonos to Santorini (approximately 2-hour high-speed ferry or 30-minute flight). Check in to your luxury caldera-view hotel in Oia or Imerovigli.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Santorini — walk along the caldera edge in Oia and find the perfect spot to witness the world-famous Santorini sunset, one of the most spectacular in the world.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast on Mykonos
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the ferry or at a café upon arrival in Santorini
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lycabettus Restaurant in Imerovigli — perched on the caldera cliff with breathtaking views; exceptional modern Greek cuisine with an extensive Santorinian wine list featuring Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance — Seajets high-speed catamaran is recommended. Hotel recommendation in Santorini: Canaves Oia Epitome or Grace Hotel Santorini for iconic caldera views and infinity pools. Oia gets very crowded at sunset — arrive early to secure a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing tour around Santorini — sail to the volcanic hot springs, the Red Beach, White Beach, and the volcanic island of Nea Kameni. Swim in the warm sulfuric waters and snorkel in crystal-clear coves. A premium private catamaran includes a gourmet lunch and open bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the catamaran tour — afternoon sailing with views of the caldera cliffs and Oia from the sea, the most dramatic perspective of Santorini. Return to port by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest village with panoramic 360-degree views of the island. Explore the medieval castle ruins and enjoy a quieter, more authentic Santorinian experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with caldera views
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on the catamaran — fresh Greek salads, grilled meats, seafood, local cheeses, and Santorinian wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — one of Santorini's most acclaimed restaurants, celebrating local Cycladic ingredients with refined modern technique; try the fava with caramelized onions and the local lamb

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran well in advance — June is peak season. Apply waterproof sunscreen. The hot springs can stain swimwear with sulfur — bring an older swimsuit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide for the full historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the Red Beach near Akrotiri — one of Santorini's most dramatic beaches with towering red volcanic cliffs. Swim in the clear waters and enjoy the unique volcanic landscape. Alternatively, visit the black sand beach of Perissa or Perivolos for a beach club experience.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting tour at Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas — Santorini is home to one of Greece's most distinctive wine regions, producing exceptional Assyrtiko white wines from ancient ungrafted vines. Enjoy a premium tasting with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Akrotiri Lighthouse Restaurant — stunning clifftop location at the southern tip of Santorini; fresh seafood and local mezedes with panoramic sea views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — a beloved local taverna known for authentic Santorinian home cooking; try the tomato keftedes (local specialty), fava, and slow-cooked rabbit

day_by_day.notes: The Red Beach requires a short walk over rocky terrain — wear sturdy sandals. Akrotiri archaeological site is covered so it's a good option even on slightly rainy days. Book the wine tasting in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Fira (Santorini's capital) — visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera housing extraordinary Akrotiri artifacts, and the Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral. Walk the caldera path from Fira to Imerovigli for spectacular views (approximately 2 hours, moderate difficulty).
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a luxury spa afternoon at your hotel — many caldera hotels offer world-class spa treatments including volcanic stone massages, Greek olive oil body treatments, and infinity pool relaxation. This is the perfect way to unwind before the final full day.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Santorini — return to Oia for a last sunset experience, then a special farewell dinner at one of the island's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Special hotel breakfast — request a private terrace setup with caldera views for a memorable morning
meals.lunch: Lunch at Roka Restaurant in Oia — charming garden restaurant with excellent fresh pasta and local Santorinian dishes
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at 1800 Restaurant in Oia — housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century captain's mansion; exceptional modern Mediterranean cuisine with an award-winning wine cellar; try the lobster risotto and the chocolate lava cake with mastiha ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Fira to Imerovigli caldera walk is one of Santorini's highlights — do it in the morning before the heat peaks. Book the spa treatment in advance. The 1800 Restaurant requires a reservation well in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Santorini — enjoy a leisurely breakfast with caldera views. Take a last walk through Oia's blue-domed churches and alleyways. Do any final souvenir shopping — local products to bring home include Santorinian Assyrtiko wine, fava (yellow split peas), capers, and local honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Santorini Airport (JTR) for your return flight. Alternatively, if the flight is in the evening, store luggage at the hotel and spend a final few hours at a caldera-view café or pool.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Santorini — fly back to Athens for a connecting flight home, or take a direct international flight if available. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through the best of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — make it special with a champagne toast to the trip
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Oia or Fira before departure — fresh tomato bruschetta, local cheese plate, and a glass of chilled Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Santorini Airport is small — arrive at least 90 minutes before departure. Purchase local products at the airport duty-free or from shops in Oia/Fira before heading to the airport. Confirm all return flight details the evening before.
